prompts.text: Which family name or nickname has a story we haven't heard in full?
Tell us about the first time you learned why somebody in our family received their name.
We find a family photograph with three unfamiliar names on the back. Who would you ask first to identify them?
A family nickname sometimes preserves more history than an official surname.
Would you rather trace the origin of our surname or collect the stories behind everyone's nicknames?
The way relatives pronounce a name sometimes reveals where they grew up.
Is there a name in our family whose meaning has changed across generations?
A younger relative asks why their name matters to the family. What story would you share with them?
Describe a time someone else's name led to an unexpected conversation about our family.
What would you want future relatives to know about how names were chosen in our family?
Which family celebration has changed the most since you were younger?
Tell us about a celebration from your childhood that we would hardly recognise today.
We have one weekend to bring relatives from different generations together. What tradition should we make room for?
The small routines before a family celebration are sometimes more meaningful than the main event.
Would you rather recreate an old family celebration exactly or introduce one new activity everyone helps choose?
Different relatives often remember different parts of the same celebration as the highlight.
What's one celebration detail our family keeps repeating without remembering how it began?
A relative who lives far away wants to join an important family occasion. How should we include them meaningfully?
Describe a family event where something unplanned became the story everyone still tells.
Which part of our family celebrations would you most like younger relatives to understand?
What ordinary task took much longer when the older members of our family were young?
Tell us about a typical school morning from a period of your life we haven't heard much about.
We spend one day living by the routines our grandparents followed at our age. What would surprise us first?
Ordinary family routines often reveal more about a generation than its biggest milestones.
Would you rather hear how relatives used to travel to school or how they spent their free afternoons?
The same household chore can mean different things to people who grew up with different tools.
What did a normal Sunday look like in our family before our current routines existed?
An old shopping list turns up in a family notebook. What might its contents tell us about daily life then?
Describe something you thought every household did until you visited another family.
What part of everyday family life today do you think future generations will find difficult to picture?
Which family dish has the most interesting story behind the person who first made it?
Tell us about learning a cooking trick from a relative who never measured ingredients.
We want to record one family recipe before the details fade. What questions should we ask the person who makes it?
A family's favourite meal is sometimes defined more by who prepares it than by its ingredients.
Would you rather cook an old family recipe together or invite everyone to bring a dish representing their own childhood?
People often remember the conversation around a family meal more clearly than the food itself.
What food did you dislike as a child but come to appreciate because of a family memory?
Two relatives insist they know the original version of the same recipe. How should we record both stories?
Describe a meal when someone shared a family story you had never heard before.
What do our usual seating arrangements or serving habits say about how family meals have changed?
What's something a younger relative taught you that changed the way you approached an everyday problem?
Tell us about advice from an older relative that made more sense years after you first heard it.
Every generation in our family gets to teach one practical skill at a gathering. What would you offer?
Learning between generations works best when everyone gets a chance to be the teacher.
Would you rather learn a childhood game from an elder or teach them a digital skill you use every day?
Relatives sometimes give the same advice using completely different examples from their own lives.
What family belief about work, money or friendship has changed as new generations have grown up?
An older relative and a younger one disagree about the best way to solve a problem. What questions might reveal where each view comes from?
Describe a time you saw two generations work together better than either expected.
Which family skill or piece of knowledge do you hope someone passes on before it's forgotten?
Which move or change of neighbourhood had the biggest influence on our family's routines?
Tell us about the first home you remember clearly and one detail that made it feel familiar.
We draw a map of every place our family has lived. What stories should we attach to each location?
The feeling of home often comes from repeated family habits rather than a particular building.
Would you rather revisit a childhood home or meet the neighbours who knew our family there?
A family can keep the same routines while the streets and houses around them change.
What did relatives miss most when they moved away from a familiar community?
A child in our family asks why we have relatives in several different cities. How would you explain the story?
Describe a moment when a new house began to feel like home because of something the family did together.
What place connected to our family history would you most like to visit and why?
Which family story do you suspect different relatives remember in completely different ways?

prompts.text: How did relatives in our family stay connected before group chats and video calls?
Tell us about a letter, phone call or visit that mattered more than the person sending it realised.
We want to keep closer contact with relatives who have different schedules and preferences. What routine would work for everyone?
Regular short conversations sometimes keep family relationships stronger than occasional elaborate gatherings.
Would you rather receive a handwritten note from a relative or hear them tell the same story in a voice recording?
Some family members show affection by checking in often while others prefer helping with practical things.
What's a question you wish relatives asked one another more often during ordinary phone calls?
An older relative doesn't enjoy texting but wants to hear family news. What other ways of sharing updates would feel natural?
Describe an unexpected message from a relative that made an ordinary day memorable.
What family communication habit should we keep even as the technology changes?
What's a small family routine we follow without calling it a tradition?
Tell us how a repeated joke, phrase or habit first became part of our household.
We want to start one simple tradition that doesn't require money or travel. What would everyone enjoy?
The traditions people remember longest are sometimes the ones nobody planned deliberately.
Would you rather preserve a familiar family game or begin an annual storytelling evening?
A habit that seems ordinary to one household can feel distinctive to visitors.
Which family tradition have you seen change its meaning as people grew older?
A new family member joins a gathering and doesn't understand one of our routines. How would you introduce it without making them uncomfortable?
Describe a moment when you realised a small household habit had become important to you.
What everyday family ritual would you want a child in the family to remember twenty years from now?
What do you hope our family will spend more time doing together over the next few years?
Tell us about a family plan from the past that changed direction and turned out well.
We put one question from every relative into a box to revisit in ten years. What would you ask?
Family plans become more useful when they leave room for people to change their minds.
Would you rather make a shared family photo archive or record short interviews with each relative?
A family's hopes for the future often look different depending on who is asked first.
What would you like younger relatives to feel free to do differently from previous generations?
Our family has to choose one project everyone contributes to in a small way. What would make it worthwhile across different ages?
Describe a time a family member supported a goal you weren't sure they would understand.
What should we ask each other now so important family stories don't remain untold?
